newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-CSR says in talks on sugar industry.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-CSR says in talks on sugar industry.

text.p: Building products, aluminium and sugar group CSR Ltd said on Monday it was in talks with other sugar producers about possible rationalisation in the Australian sugar industry.

"We are in talks," CSR executive general manager of sugar Peter Frawley told reporters after a briefing on the company's first half results. Asked if CSR was in talks with Mackay Refined Sugars, Frawley repiled: "Yes, Mackay, everyone."
CSR managing director Geoffrey Kells told reporters after the briefing the company hoped there would be some rationalisation in Australia's white sugar market.

"We would hope there would be industry rationalisation," Kells told reporters. He said local sugar companies had told the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) that the current sugar price war situation was untenable.
"The ACCC is unaware that individual companies are in discussions with one another about ways to rationalise the industry," Frawley said.
Mackay is a joint venture between international commodities firm E D & F Man.
CSR, Mackay and fellow refiner Manildra Harwood, control about 90 percent of the Australasian white sugar markets.
CSR earlier reported a 24 percent fall in net profit to A$154.7 million for the six months ended September 30, 1996.
CSR shares closed 10 cents lower at A$4.18.
